title: Video showcase
summary: Nouns and verbs for a truthful demo video: script, storyboard, shot list, capture plan, media, sequence, captions, evidence links and tool cards, with verbs from script to QA and review.
boundaries: Use only synthetic or demo data on screen. No credentials, real personal data, private tabs or notifications may appear in any capture.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.
Narration is recorded by a person; any generated media is labeled.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

value.lets_workers: Make a truthful demo video as ordinary claimed work: script, storyboard, screen capture, human narration, captions, rendering, assembly in 16:9 with an optional 9:16 cut, automatic QA and review, where every on-screen number links to its evidence.

flow.when: First, from the requester's video brief.
After the script; produces the storyboard, shot list and capture plan.
Per capture in the plan; captures can run as separate attempts.
A person records the script; no model is used.
For storyboard scenes that are rendered rather than captured.
After media, narration and captions exist.
Last, by a person or a different worker.

kinema_alignment.status: Kinema is being extended on a separate branch with 16:9 output, media and sequence nouns, and render and QA verbs. Nothing here depends on that work landing.

shared_words.scene recipe: Kinema's noun.scene_recipe; render-scenes hands rendered scenes to Kinema's deterministic renderer when it is available.
shared_words.media: A hash-pinned recording, image or audio file, the same meaning Kinema uses.
shared_words.sequence: The ordered clips with cuts and crossfades that assemble encodes, the same meaning Kinema uses.
shared_words.render: Deterministic frame production with no model call per frame.
shared_words.QA: Post-encode checks: black and frozen frames, loudness, captions, format and frame-hash spot checks.

value.privacy: Use only synthetic or demo data on screen. No credentials, real personal data, private tabs or notifications may appear in any capture.
value.publication: Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

nouns.title: Demo video style guide
nouns.category_reason: A reusable production method with its guardrails, read by every verb in this pack.

value.defaults_note: These are adjustable defaults. The requester's video brief overrides them.

formats.primary: 16:9 at 1920x1080, 30 frames per second, H.264 (yuv420p) with AAC audio at 48 kHz.
formats.captions: A sidecar caption file (SRT or WebVTT) always; burned-in captions when the brief asks for them.

content_rules: Show the real product working with synthetic or demo data.
Every number on screen links to its evidence: a test run, a counts record, an event log, a receipt or a dated public source.
Label any generated still, voice or clip as generated.
Prefer a human narrator reading the script in their own voice.
One idea per beat; plain words; no claims the evidence does not support.
caption_rules: At most 2 lines per cue and 42 characters per line.
Each cue on screen for 1 to 7 seconds.
Keep captions inside the inner 90 percent of the frame.
audio_rules: Integrated loudness about -16 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP for web playback.
Music, if any, stays well under the narration.
value.privacy: Use only synthetic or demo data on screen. No credentials, real personal data, private tabs or notifications may appear in any capture.

nouns.title: Video QA checks, thresholds and commands
nouns.category_reason: A fixed set of deterministic checks with thresholds and reproducible commands, used to score every assembled output.

checks.threshold: No black segment of 0.5 s or longer except declared fades.
No frozen segment of 2 s or longer except declared holds.
Integrated loudness -16 LUFS plus or minus 1 LU; true peak at most -1 dBTP.
1920x1080 for 16:9 or 1080x1920 for 9:16, the declared frame rate, H.264 with yuv420p, AAC at 48 kHz.
Within 5 percent of the brief's target_seconds.
Cues cover at least 95 percent of narration speech time.
checks.method: Compare cue intervals with the narration take's speech segments from the transcript.

checks.threshold: At most 2 lines, at most 42 characters per line, at most 17 characters per second.
checks.method: Deterministic check over the caption track.

checks.threshold: Spot frames of rendered scenes match the render manifest's frame digests.
checks.method: Extract the same frame indexes and compare SHA-256 digests of decoded frames.

checks.threshold: Every claim id in the script has an evidence link with result verified.
checks.method: Deterministic join of script claims and evidence links.

checks.threshold: Every media noun with generated true is labeled on screen or in the description.
checks.method: Deterministic join of sequence clips and media nouns, plus a visual check.

rules: Every check reports its measurement, not only pass or fail.
A check that cannot run is not_run with the reason, never pass.
Thresholds come from the style guide unless the brief overrides them; record which applied.

nouns.title: Tool card: FFmpeg
nouns.category_reason: A tool card pins an external executable's identity, license and required capabilities for verbs that invoke it.

value.name: FFmpeg

tool_license.how_to_determine: Run ffmpeg -hide_banner -version and ffmpeg -hide_banner -L, and record the configuration line and the license text they print.

value.pin_reason: Pin the exact build a worker uses: version string, configuration line and the binary's SHA-256. This card names no build.
required_capabilities: subtitles filter (needs libass) for burned-in captions
checks: ffprobe reports the expected streams for a 2-second synthetic test clip made by the same build.
value.install_policy: This card installs nothing. A worker uses an already qualified build or prepares one in its own workspace under its task's execution policy.

nouns.title: Tool card: Playwright
nouns.category_reason: A tool card pins a library's identity, license and use for verbs that invoke it.

value.name: Playwright
value.pin_reason: Pin the exact Playwright version; it also fixes the browser build it downloads.
uses: Scripted screen capture at a fixed viewport from a capture plan.
Rasterizing SVG scene frames to PNG for assembly.
cautions: Check the built-in video recording's codec, frame rate and sharpness before relying on it; timed screenshots or a platform screen recorder may give crisper results.
Use a fresh browser profile with no signed-in accounts.
value.install_policy: This card installs nothing; browser downloads happen only under the worker's own execution policy.
checks: Capture a 2-second recording of a local static page at 1920x1080 and confirm its dimensions with ffprobe.

nouns.title: Tool card: Chromium
nouns.category_reason: A tool card pins a browser's identity and license for the capture and rasterization verbs.

value.name: Chromium

tool_license.note: BSD-3-Clause covers Chromium's own code. Bundled third-party components carry their own licenses, listed on the build's chrome://credits page; record that list for the exact build.

value.pin_reason: Use the browser build fixed by the pinned Playwright version and record its version string.

verbs.title: Draft the script
verbs.summary: Write a timed narration script from the video brief, listing every on-screen number as a claim with an id.
verbs.outcome: A private script noun and one unverified evidence-link draft per claim.

slots.name: video_brief
slots.description: Pin of the requester's video brief.

steps: Verify the brief pin. Read the style guide.
Write beats in plain words, one idea per beat, within the brief's target length.
List every number that will be spoken or shown as a claim with an id. Draft its evidence link from the brief's evidence sources with result unverified.
Leave a claim out rather than include a number you cannot trace.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

acceptance.check: The script validates against template.script's schema.
Beat durations sum to total_seconds within 5 percent, and total_seconds is within 10 percent of the brief's target.
Every claim id has exactly one evidence-link draft.
A viewer from the brief's audience can follow each beat.

verbs.title: Storyboard the video
verbs.summary: Turn the script into scenes, a shot list and a capture plan that a capture worker and a renderer can follow exactly.
verbs.outcome: Private storyboard, shot-list and capture-plan nouns.
steps: Verify the pins. Map every beat to at least one scene.
Prefer real screen captures of the working product; use rendered scenes for titles, diagrams and transitions.
Write a capture plan step by step with viewport 1920x1080, synthetic or demo data and privacy checks.
Mark which shots need a 9:16 variant when the brief asks for one.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

acceptance.check: Storyboard, shot list and capture plan validate against their templates.
Every beat id appears in a scene, and every scene has a shot.
Every screen_capture shot has a capture plan entry with privacy checks.
A capture worker could follow each capture without guessing.

verbs.title: Capture the screen
verbs.summary: Run the capture plan's scripted steps against local or demo targets and store each recording as a hash-pinned media noun.
verbs.outcome: One private media noun per capture, each with its digest, dimensions and duration.

capture_ids.description: Captures to run in this attempt. Empty means all.

steps: Verify the pins and the pinned Playwright and Chromium builds before running anything.
Use a fresh browser profile, signed out of every account, with notifications off.
Run each capture's steps exactly, at its viewport, against its local or demo target only.
Store each recording as a blob, compute its SHA-256, and write a media noun with generated false.
Stop and return blocked if any frame would show a credential, real personal data or an unplanned site.

acceptance.check: Every media noun validates against template.media's schema.
Each media noun's blob digest equals the SHA-256 of the stored bytes.
Width and height match the capture plan's viewport times its scale factor.
A frame-by-frame skim shows no credential, personal data or unplanned site.

verbs.network: Only the local or demo targets named in the capture plan. No other sites, accounts or services.
capabilities: a qualified Playwright and Chromium build
notes: A person may claim this verb and record the plan by hand; the media noun and checks are the same.

verbs.title: Record the narration
verbs.summary: A person reads the script in their own voice and uploads the take; no model is involved.
verbs.outcome: A private narration media noun, or no_change if the person decides to keep an earlier take.

slots.name: script
slots.description: Pin of the script to read.

steps: Read the script aloud in a quiet room; small departures from the script are fine and will be captured by transcription.
Record at 48 kHz, mono or stereo, without music.
Upload the take as a private blob and write a media noun with kind narration and generated false.
Nobody else's voice and no synthetic voice is used in this verb.

acceptance.check: The narration noun validates against template.media's schema with kind narration.
The blob digest equals the SHA-256 of the stored bytes.
generated is false.
The take is clear enough to transcribe.

verbs.title: Transcribe captions
verbs.summary: Transcribe the narration into timed captions and list where the speech differs from the script.
verbs.outcome: A private caption track that follows the style guide's caption rules.

slots.name: narration
slots.description: Pin of the narration media noun.

steps: Verify the pins and the narration blob's digest.
Transcribe with the speech-to-text tool or model your allowance permits; record which one in the execution report.
Split cues by the style guide's caption rules and align them to the audio.
List each difference between script and speech instead of silently correcting it.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

acceptance.check: The caption track validates against template.caption-track's schema.
Every cue has at most 2 lines, 42 characters per line and 17 characters per second.
Cues are in time order, do not overlap and end before the narration ends.
Captions match what was said, not what the script hoped.

verbs.title: Render scenes
verbs.summary: Render the storyboard's title cards, diagrams and transitions deterministically and record frame digests.
verbs.outcome: Private media nouns for each rendered scene and a render manifest with digests.

slots.name: scene_recipes
slots.description: Optional pins of Kinema scene recipes for rendered shots.

steps: Verify every pin and every tool build before rendering.
Render only rendered_scene and title_card shots. Use Kinema's deterministic renderer for pinned scene recipes when it is installed and qualified.
Use no model per frame. Record frame counts, sizes and spot-frame digests in the render manifest.
Render the 9:16 variant only for shots that list it.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

acceptance.check: The render manifest validates against its template and model_calls is 0.
Rendering one scene twice yields identical spot-frame digests.
Each output matches its aspect's dimensions.
Rendered scenes match the storyboard's intent.

verbs.title: Assemble and encode
verbs.summary: Cut the media into the storyboard's sequence with crossfades, mix the narration, attach captions and encode 16:9 and the optional 9:16 output.
verbs.outcome: A private sequence noun and encoded output media with digests.

slots.name: media
slots.description: Pins of captured and rendered media.

slots.name: narration
slots.description: Pin of the narration media noun.

burn_in_captions.description: Burn captions into the picture in addition to the sidecar file.

steps: Verify every pin and every media blob digest before cutting.
Build the timeline from the storyboard: cuts and crossfades only, in storyboard order.
Mix narration to the style guide's loudness target, attach the sidecar captions and burn them in only when asked.
Encode each requested aspect with the pinned FFmpeg build and record each output's digest and format.
Keep every output private. Publishing, uploading or posting the video is the owner's separate decision.

acceptance.check: The sequence validates against template.sequence's schema.
Every clip references a pinned media noun whose digest was verified.
Every encoded output has a media noun with its digest, size, frame rate and codec.
Cuts and crossfades land on beat boundaries.

verbs.title: Check the encoded video
verbs.summary: Run every QA check on one encoded output: black and frozen frames, loudness, format, duration, captions, frame spot checks, evidence coverage and generated-media labels.
verbs.outcome: A private QA report with a measurement for every check.

slots.name: encoded_output
slots.description: Pin of one encoded output media noun.

slots.name: script
slots.description: Pin of the script, for claim ids.

slots.name: render_manifest
slots.description: Pin of the render manifest, if scenes were rendered.

steps: Verify the pins and the output blob's digest.
Run each check in qa-thresholds with the pinned FFmpeg build and record its measurement.
Mark a check not_run with its reason when it cannot run; never mark it pass.
Set passed to true only when every check passed.

acceptance.check: The QA report validates against template.qa-report's schema.
Every check id in qa-thresholds appears exactly once.
passed is true exactly when every check result is pass.

verbs.title: Review the cut
verbs.summary: A person or a different worker watches the cut with its QA report and evidence links and decides whether it is ready for the owner.
verbs.outcome: Private review notes with a decision; publishing remains the owner's separate act.

slots.name: encoded_output
slots.description: Pin of the encoded output to review.

steps: Confirm you did not assemble this cut; if you did, return blocked.
Watch the whole cut. Check each claim against its evidence link.
Check rights and labels for every generated or third-party asset.
Decide ready_for_owner_decision, revise or reject. Never publish.

acceptance.check: The review notes validate against template.review-notes's schema.
Every claim id in the script has a review result.
A ready decision requires a QA report with passed true.
The video makes its point clearly for the brief's audience.
